articles.title: The Ferran Torres Era? How a shocking stat puts the PSG winger ahead of Messi and Mbappé
articles.standfirst: He delivers the most explosive debut in recent history
articles.summary: He delivers the most explosive debut in recent history
articles.body:
Two goals in his first minutes wearing the Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) shirt. No one, not Neymar, Mbappé or Messi , had had such a prolific debut as Ferran Torres , who, this Sunday against Rennes (2-2), matched the two best goalscoring debuts in the history of his new club.

Swede Zlatan Ibrahimovic , in his first match with the Parisians in 2012, and Cameroonian Patrick Mboma , in 1994, had also scored two goals in their debuts with PSG , the French newspaper L"Équipe recalled this Monday.

The charismatic Ibrahimovic , PSG's legendary goalscorer, for whom he scored 156 goals in 180 matches between 2012 and 2016 , netted, on August 11, 2012 against Lorient, two goals that helped level a 0-2 deficit.

Precisely, the two goals by the forward who gave Spain its second World Cup also served this time to level a 0-2 deficit, with two moves in the 71st and 82nd minutes, from passes by his national team teammate and also world champion, Fabián Ruiz .

The former Barcelona and Manchester City player had replaced 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé at halftime, while Ruiz came on in the 59th minute for the Portuguese Joao Neves.

Grateful to the club, his teammates, and Luis Enrique

"Before coming, I had already been told it was a magnificent group, but until you're inside, you don't realize it (...) There are only good people, good players. The truth is that I feel very fortunate to be able to play with them ," said the Spanish hero of the World Cup final against Argentina after the match.

The natural striker from Foios (Valencia) also thanked his main supporter at the Parisian club, Spanish coach Luis Enrique , whom he knows very well from their time together in the Spanish national team.

First of all, I thank him for signing me . He is a coach who has always given me a lot of confidence. He has always conveyed his trust in me, and I hope to repay him," he said.

Luis Enrique, who has taken PSG to the top of European football with two consecutive Champions Leagues (2025 and 2026), responded to the performance of his protégé, whom he gave his debut with Spain in September 2020.

It wasn't bad, was it? He scored two goals (2-2), but I'm happy with everyone who came on in a very difficult match, because we had a lot of difficulties controlling Rennes in the first half (...) for me it is important to see that there are so many players ready

articles.title: Can PSG win a third straight Champions League? Luis Enrique’s side has a real shot at history
articles.standfirst: The road ahead for the European powerhouse will be anything but easy
articles.summary: The road ahead for the European powerhouse will be anything but easy
articles.body:
Winning the UEFA Champions League once is difficult. Winning it twice in a row is rarer still. Winning it three consecutive times would place a club among the greatest dynasties European soccer has ever seen.

That is the challenge facing Paris Saint-Germain as the French giants begin another Champions League campaign after capturing back-to-back European crowns under Luis Enrique.

Can PSG make history and win a third successive title?

The answer is yes, but the road ahead will be anything but easy. For years, PSG entered every Champions League season burdened by expectations and haunted by disappointment. That narrative has changed dramatically.

Luis Enrique has transformed the club from a collection of stars into one of Europe's most complete teams.

PSG has developed a clear tactical identity built around pressing, possession, and collective discipline. The results speak for themselves. Back-to-back Champions League triumphs have established PSG as the team everyone else is chasing. More importantly, the squad has shown an ability to handle the pressure that comes with being a favorite.

Champions League campaigns are often decided by a handful of moments in hostile stadiums, knockout-round adversity, and a team's ability to remain composed when everything is on the line. PSG has already navigated those challenges twice.

The draw is challenging but manageable

The newly released schedule provides several intriguing tests.

PSG's home fixtures include matchups against Barcelona, Roma, Galatasaray, and Slovan Bratislava. On paper, Barcelona represents the headline opponent. The Spanish giants remain one of Europe's most talented clubs and will provide an early measuring stick for PSG's title credentials.

Roma and Galatasaray are capable of creating difficult tactical battles, while Slovan Bratislava is the type of opponent that champions must dispatch efficiently. The away schedule may prove even more interesting.

Trips to Villarreal, Como, Manchester City, and Aston Villa ensure that PSG will face a variety of playing styles and atmospheres.

The visit to City immediately stands out as one of the toughest fixtures any team could draw. Villa Park has become one of the most intimidating venues in Europe under Unai Emery, while Villarreal's European pedigree makes them a dangerous opponent regardless of form. The schedule is demanding, but it is not overwhelming. However, PSG has faced tougher paths before.

Luis Enrique sounds relaxed

Perhaps the most encouraging sign for PSG supporters is the demeanor of their manager. Speaking after the draw, Luis Enrique joked about his previous experiences watching Champions League pairings unfold.

"In my first three years here, I watched it from my office, and it was a disaster each time as we got drawn against the toughest teams," he said.

Rather than obsessing over potential opponents, the coach revealed that he planned to spend the day cycling around Paris while club executives Olivier Gagne and Luís Campos monitored the proceedings. "It can't be any worse than last year," Enrique said with a laugh. "When we get home, we'll see what we've got ahead of us, but I'll happily take the end result of the last two seasons."

Those comments reflect a manager who understands that PSG's focus should be on itself rather than the draw. When a team has won consecutive Champions League trophies, confidence becomes a competitive advantage. The biggest obstacle to a third straight title may not be the schedule, but fatigue.

The modern soccer calendar is more demanding than ever, particularly for players who participated in the World Cup and other international competitions. Luis Enrique acknowledged that reality when discussing his squad management approach. "I'm always open to giving a few days off to the players who came back less rested because they'd played at the World Cup, " he explained. "It's important to disconnect."
